title: Bleeding
steps: Apply firm, direct pressure with a clean cloth or gauze.
Do not remove the cloth — add more on top if soaked through.
Keep your pet calm and still.
If bleeding does not slow within 5 minutes, go to the emergency vet.

title: Difficulty Breathing
steps: Keep your pet as calm and still as possible.
Do not muzzle your pet.
Minimize handling and transport carefully.
Go to the emergency vet immediately — do not wait.

title: Mild Vomiting
steps: Withhold food for 6–12 hours (if adult and otherwise healthy).
Offer small amounts of water frequently.
Reintroduce bland food slowly (boiled chicken and rice).
If vomiting continues more than 24 hours, contact your vet.

title: Minor Limp
steps: Restrict activity and keep your pet rested.
Check the paw for debris or injury.
Avoid giving human medications.
If limping lasts more than 24–48 hours, see your vet.

title: Seizure
steps: Do not restrain your pet or put your hands near their mouth.
Clear the area of hard or sharp objects.
Time the seizure — if over 5 minutes, go to the ER immediately.
Keep the room quiet and dim.
After the seizure, keep your pet warm and calm.
Contact your vet even if the seizure stops on its own.

title: Toxic Food or Poison
steps: Do NOT induce vomiting unless directed by a vet.
Identify the substance if possible and note the amount ingested.
Call ASPCA Poison Control: 1-888-426-4435.
Go to the emergency vet immediately.
